A_target.statement:
Let $X_1, \ldots, X_n$ be [[Definition:Independent Random Variables|independent random variables]] and $S_n = \displaystyle \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n X_i$.
Then for all $s > 0$:
:$\displaystyle \map \Pr {S_n - \expect {S_n} \ge a} \le e^{-s a} \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \expect {e^{s \paren {X_i - \expect {X_i} } } }$

B_source.statement:
Let $Z$ be a [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]] and $s > 0$.
Then:
:$\map \Pr {Z \ge a} \le e^{-s a} \expect {e^{s Z} }$

derived.the Chernoff bound: the product form of the sum tail bound

validity_conditions: Apply Chernoff to Z = S_n - E[S_n], giving P(Z >= a) <= e^{-sa} E[e^{sZ}].
By independence of the X_i, e^{sZ} = prod e^{s(X_i - E X_i)} factorizes: E[e^{sZ}] = prod_i E[e^{s(X_i - E X_i)}].
This is the standard first step of Hoeffding's inequality (before bounding each MGF factor).
proof_plan: Let $Z = S_n - \expect {S_n}$ and apply the [[Chernoff Bound]].

This gives:
:$\map \Pr {Z \ge a} \le e^{-s a} \expect {e^{s Z} }$

As the $X_i$ are [[Definition:Independent Random Variables|independent]], so are the $e^{s \paren {X_i - \expect {X_i} } }$.
By [[Expectation of Product of Independent Random Variables]]:
:$\displaystyle \expect {e^{s Z} } = \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \expect {e^{s \paren {X_i - \expect {X_i} } } }$

Hence:
:$\displaystyle \map \Pr {S_n - \expect {S_n} \ge a} \le e^{-s a} \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \expect {e^{s \paren {X_i - \expect {X_i} } } }$
which is the setup for [[Hoeffding's Inequality]].
{{qed}}
